_source: AI-researched NEW DISTRICT candidates for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly promoted by the research agent. Populated by the same daily scheduled research agent as venue-suggestions.json (2026-08, at explicit user request), committed straight to master the same way (see that file's own doc comment for why). Expected to be rare: the research brief (.claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md) treats district suggestions as an occasional finding (a genuinely distinct, not-yet-covered high-end area within Manchester or Cheshire), not a daily quota — most days should add zero entries here. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) is the only thing that promotes an entry into the real docs/data/districts.json, behind its own pull request. Each entry mirrors docs/data/districts.json's own raw shape (name/metro/lat/lon/base/kind/accentColor/editorialDescription) so an approved entry can be copied straight in, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) stripped on promotion. `metro` must be 'manchester' or 'cheshire' only — never 'los-angeles' or a new metro (out of scope, per the user's explicit 'shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet').
_reviewWorkflow: Same as venue-suggestions.json: status starts 'pending', the review agent flips it to 'approved' (then copies fields into districts.json, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (kept here with researchNotes so it isn't re-suggested). A human's real review happens by reading/merging that PR.

suggestions.name: Bramhall
suggestions.editorialDescription: A village green with a Tudor manor behind it and a shopping parade in front — the sort of Stockport postcode that would rather be mistaken for Cheshire, and mostly gets away with it.
suggestions.researchNotes: A genuine, well-known, distinct Stockport village (I Love Bramhall, manchestersfinest.com, adamsimms.exp.uk.com all describe it as a real, independent-heavy village centre with its own identity) that doesn't overlap any existing district — closest neighbour is Cheadle Hulme, roughly 2.6km away (Bramhall Lane South's SK7 1AL postcode centroid at 53.357874/-2.165865 vs Cheadle Hulme's 53.3761/-2.1897), a comparable real-world gap to already-accepted close pairs like Heaton Moor/Stockport (Underbanks). Passes the brief's own sanity check: a Cheshire/Manchester local would reasonably expect Bramhall on a 'best of' list alongside Cheadle Hulme and Heaton Moor, both of which are already covered. Anchored by Bramall Hall (a genuine Grade I-listed Tudor manor house and public park, Wikipedia/own council listing), with its own high street (Moss Lane/Bramhall Lane South, home to Bramhall's own indie bookshop-cafe-wine-bar and several independent restaurants per manchestersfinest.com and Tripadvisor's own Bramhall listings). Administratively part of the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport, Greater Manchester, not the historic county of Cheshire — assigned metro 'cheshire' anyway on the same real historic-county-identity and leafy/suburban-character judgment already made for the adjacent Cheadle Hulme (see docs/data/districts.json's own note on that district), rather than the 'manchester'-as-Greater-Manchester-shorthand judgment used for Stockport (Underbanks) and Heaton Moor, whose regeneration/urban-terrace character reads differently. base (46) set just above Cheadle Hulme's (42), reflecting a comparably sized but slightly busier village centre; no curated venues researched yet — this is a district-only proposal, same starting point every prior district suggestion has had before its own first venue pass. accentColor (#7D6B87, muted heather-plum) checked for perceptual distinctness against every existing accent — closest neighbours are Northern Quarter's plum (#8B6FA8, notably more blue/saturated) and Didsbury's dusty rose (#B98098, notably pinker/warmer) — distinct from both.
